local_facts.title: A 1976 median, and six in ten homes older than 1980
local_facts.claim: The Census Bureau's American Community Survey 2024 five-year estimates count 20,359 housing units in Wheaton, with a median year built of 1976. The 1970s alone account for 5,765 of them, the largest single decade. In all, 12,650 units, about 62 percent, were built before 1980, and 1,805 date from 1939 or earlier.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A house from the 1970s has run its original ductwork through roughly fifty heating seasons, usually with several furnace swaps bolted onto the same trunk lines. Old panned returns, abandoned branches and patched joints are where debris collects, and they are the parts a supply-only cleaning never reaches.

local_facts.title: Close to six thousand heating degree days a year
local_facts.claim: National Weather Service Chicago's 1991-2020 normals for O'Hare, the official Chicago station about 13 miles northeast of Wheaton, list 5,974 heating degree days a year. January carries 1,234 of them and December 1,069, and the station averages 121 days a year with a low at or below freezing. The same normals list 1,003 cooling degree days, so the ducts also carry air-conditioned air through the summer.
local_facts.why_it_matters: From October into April the furnace blower pulls the whole house's air through the return side again and again. A loaded filter, a dusty blower wheel or a gap in a return duct gets months of runtime to make itself felt, and the same ductwork then carries the cooling load all summer.

local_facts.title: City inspections end before the drywall dust starts
local_facts.claim: The City of Wheaton's basement remodeling guideline lists underground plumbing, rough framing, rough mechanical, rough electrical and rough plumbing inspections, conducted once all rough-ins are complete but before insulation or concealment, followed by an insulation inspection once insulation and air sealing are done and before drywall, and then a final. Submittals include a floor plan with the electrical layout and escape window and a combustion air calculation worksheet.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Taping and sanding happen after the last rough inspection, and nothing on the list looks inside the ductwork. If the furnace ran while joint compound was sanded, the return side pulled the powder in, and it stays in the return trunk, the blower and the coil until somebody removes it.

local_facts.title: A furnace swap is permitted work, with a CO alarm rule attached
local_facts.claim: The City of Wheaton's residential furnace and air conditioner guideline asks for the brand, efficiency and BTU rating of the proposed furnace, the manufacturer's installation specifications, and a combustion air calculation worksheet if the appliance is gas-fired and not high-efficiency. The city's code requires carbon monoxide alarms when additions, alterations or repairs requiring a permit occur in a dwelling with a fuel-fired appliance or an attached garage that opens into the home.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A blower cleaning sometimes turns up a furnace that is near the end, and a replacement is a permitted, inspected job in Wheaton. Knowing that up front, including the CO alarm requirement it triggers, keeps a cleaning visit from sliding into unpermitted furnace work.
